thread:
maya: quick question — if we need to flip the "user-side-cache" feature flag fully OFF in prod as an emergency kill switch, who is allowed to do that and what exact steps should we follow? hit during a canary rollout this morning.

tj: oncall (current rotation) or eng-sre leads can perform a full-prod flip. PMs/product cannot. process is: 1) open an incident ticket (INC-####), 2) get a second sign-off (sre lead or eng manager) for global kills, 3) run the disable call, 4) verify metrics, 5) record audit entry. :lock:

samir: add to tj — for any flag that affects >10% traffic we require two-person verification (operator + approver). include the incident ID in the API call body so the audit trail links back. also note: prefer canary->partial rollbacks before full-off unless latency/5xx spike requires immediate off.

tj: copy — example commands (internal flags API):
```
# disable globally
POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/user-side-cache/disable
Headers: Authorization: Bearer $FLAGS_OP_TOKEN
Body: {"scope":"prod","operator":"tj","incident":"INC-2023-XXXX"}

# re-enable
POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/user-side-cache/enable
Body: {"scope":"prod","operator":"tj","incident":"INC-2023-XXXX"}
```

alex: quick verification checklist after flipping:
- watch 5xx rate (+/- 1m window)
- p50/p95 latency for inference API
- queue depth and consumer lag
- user-facing error funnel in Sentry
If metrics still bad or the disable call times out, page eng-sre and then page oncall manager. escalate to platform lead if >30m without resolution. :eyes:

maya: where do we confirm the audit entry shows up? need to hand this to compliance if they ask.

ops-bot: Flag change recorded — flag: user-side-cache, action: disable, actor: tj, scope: prod, incident: INC-2023-XXXX, audit_id: AUD-20240312-789, recorded_at: 2024-03-12T18:43:22Z. (This is an automated audit log entry.)

samir: that ops-bot line is the canonical proof. also paste the incident URL in the audit comment and add the Slack thread link. record the approver (sre_lead) in the audit fields.

tj: final practical note — if you're doing a scoped kill (region or customer subset), use the "scope" param instead of global. always include `operator` and `incident` in the body. if anyone flips without following these steps, we will revert the change and follow up via postmortem. :white_check_mark:
